subtopic: Comparing Fund Trading and Redemption Methods
source_evidence:
Mutual Funds	Once a day at close of business at NAV from fund
Exchange-Traded Funds	Intraday at market prices on a national securities exchange
Exchange-Traded Closed-End Funds	Intraday at market prices on a national securities exchange
Interval Funds	Every three, six, or twelve months at NAV from fund
answer: Fund trading and redemption methods differ in both timing and pricing. Mutual funds process transactions once a day at the close of business using the fund’s NAV. ETFs and exchange-traded closed-end funds trade intraday on a national securities exchange at market prices. Interval funds instead offer periodic repurchases—every three, six, or twelve months—at NAV from the fund. An interval fund’s repurchase offer is not the same as being able to sell whenever you choose: the fund buys back only a limited percentage of its outstanding shares, so it may not repurchase all the shares shareholders request.
